title.official: Third party statement of defence and additional options

division.heading: Actions Started by Statement of Claim

operative_text.controlling:
3.49(1)  A statement of defence by a third party defendant
(a) must be in Form 17,
(b) must comply with the rules about pleadings in Part 13,
Division 3, and
(c) may dispute either or both of the following:
(i) the defendant’s liability to the plaintiff, or
(ii) the third party defendant’s liability described in the
third party claim.
(2)  If a third party defendant files a statement of defence, the third
party defendant must file it and serve it on each of the other parties
within the applicable time after service of the third party claim on
the third party defendant.
(3)  The applicable time is
(a) 20 days if service is effected in Alberta,
(b) one month if service is effected outside Alberta but in
Canada, and
(c) 2 months if service is effected outside Canada.
(4)  A third party defendant may do either or both of the following:
(a) make a claim against a third party co-defendant in
accordance with rule 3.43;
(b) make a counterclaim in accordance with rule 3.56(2).

BOOK_A.commentary:
On the time to defend, see R.3.31. A third party could not object that the defendant had consented to judgment by the plaintiff

against the defendant, if the third party never denied the defendant's liability and had no right to a trial of that:res judicata. Whether there is a duty of care or not, need not be the same toward upstream producers and downstream consumers.

A third party is clearly a "party" for questioning (examination for discovery) purposes, but whether it is an adverse party depends on the pleadings on the particular issue.Adversity is necessary to have questioning (examination for discovery) at all, but if there is adversity then one still has to go onto the second question of what topics are relevant and material.If the third party does not challenge the plaintiff's claim, the third party cannot be questioned (examined for discovery) about that.

*Demand for Notice byThird Party Defendant*

BOOK_B.title: Third party statement of defence

commentary.text: Rule 3.49 See Alberta Rules of Court, Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.49. 1. Reason for Rule It is not difficult to understand the reason for the existence of the rule. The application of it prevents a defendant who may have nothing to lose by admitting liability from doing so to the prejudice of the third party who is the one who is ultimately liable … I believe that the parties who might be potentially ultimately liable should be given a full opportunity to defend both the defendants' claim against the third party, and the plaintiff's cliam against the defendant, regardless of whether the defendant admits liability to the plaintiff. I believe that this is the intention of the rule. Edmonton Savings & Credit Union Ltd. v. Wruk (1986), 45 Alta. L.R. (2d) 285 at 287-88 (Master).
